q: The direction of the orbital magnetic moment of a revolving electron is
why: Since the electron's charge is negative, its magnetic moment is opposite in direction to its angular momentum.

q: The smallest unit of orbital magnetic moment of an electron is called
why: Bohr magneton mu_B = eh/(4 pi m) is the fundamental quantum of orbital magnetic moment.

q: Magnetic intensity H in a solenoid depends only on
o: the external current and coil geometry
why: H is produced solely by the external current/coil, independent of the material inside.

Which of the following correctly describes diamagnetic materials?
why: Diamagnetic materials have small negative susceptibility and are weakly repelled by a magnetic field.

q: Which type of magnetic material shows a hysteresis loop and retains magnetism after the field is removed?
why: Only ferromagnetic materials show hysteresis and retentivity due to domain alignment.

q: According to Curie's law, the susceptibility chi of a paramagnetic material is
why: chi = C/T, so susceptibility decreases as temperature increases due to thermal agitation.

q: A paramagnetic material has chi = 0.004 at T = 300 K. Its new susceptibility at T = 600 K is
why: Curie constant C = chi x T = 1.2; at 600 K, chi = C/T = 1.2/600 = 0.002.

q: In a B-H hysteresis loop, the reverse magnetic field needed to bring B back to zero is called
why: Coercivity is the reverse field strength required to demagnetize the material (bring B to zero).
